Intended use: Compare algorithms on a declared benchmark
Directly interpretable comparison: Compare predictions on the same target, test members and metric after model selection outside the test set
Further comparison for a broader claim: Test on a new source or negative population for transport to that setting
References: Walsh et al., 2021; Kapoor et al., 2024; Cawley and Talbot, 2010

Directly interpretable comparison: Assay the selected candidates; measure response across a sampled ordering to assess ranking
Further comparison for a broader claim: Sample deprioritized candidates and a relevant alternative selection for error rates or enrichment
References: Guan et al., 2023; Cheng et al., 2025; Walsh et al., 2021

Intended use: Predict numerical potency under defined conditions
Directly interpretable comparison: Compare predicted potency with independent concentration–response measurements and numerical errors
Further comparison for a broader claim: Assess calibration after a change in assay, material or endpoint
References: Nongonierma and FitzGerald, 2016; Zan et al., 2023

Intended use: Claim an added effect in a processed food
Directly interpretable comparison: Compare the specified endpoint with a matched processed matrix or formulation control
Further comparison for a broader claim: Attribute the effect to a peptide and test additional endpoints or human outcomes with corresponding experiments
References: Yao et al., 2026; Tenenbaum et al., 2023
